subject: Execution footprint & deletion assurances for CivicBank — evidence packet requested
messages:
From: Alice Grant <alice.grant@civicbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Quick clarification: where do requests actually run and how are they deleted?

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — CivicBank’s security and procurement teams asked for a short write-up we can present to our InfoSec committee. Two focused asks:

1) For the hosted API and Dedicated modes, where are inference requests executed (region-level) and which subcontractors/subprocessors touch request data in transit or at rest? We need a concise map (regions, cloud providers, subprocessor names).
2) What is the default retention and deletion behavior for model inputs, KV cache, and operational logs? Do you provide evidence (subprocessor inventory, processing map, SOC2) we can attach to our internal packet?

If possible, send a short PDF we can attach to the committee deck and an inventory CSV for our vendor manager.

Regards,
Alice Grant
Head of Security Governance
CivicBank

P.S. cc’ing Jorge from our compliance partner who will help validate the artifacts.

--

Attachment: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Grant <alice.grant@civicbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jorge Ruiz <jorge@complyworks.io>
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: where do requests actually run and how are they deleted?

Hi Alice,

Thanks — great questions and very timely. High-level answers below; I’ve attached a short summary PDF and will loop Marissa in with the subprocessor inventory and a technical map.

- Execution regions: Hosted API defaults to nearest-region routing (US/EU/APAC) based on request origin. We maintain capacity in primary regions (US-EAST-1, EU-WEST-1, APAC-SOUTHEAST-1) and can pin customers to a specific region under Dedicated or Private deployments.

- Subprocessors: For Hosted we rely on cloud infra providers (AWS/GCP) and a small set of managed services for logging and observability. Dedicated customers can require an allowlist and Private deployments avoid our hosted subprocessor list entirely. Full vendor inventory is attached.

- Retention & deletion: By default, transient model state (KV cache) lives only for the session and is purged after 24–48 hours unless you enable session persist. Customer request payloads (for hosted accounts) are retained for up to 30 days to support rate-limiting and customer support workflows; long-term logs (aggregated telemetry) are retained 90 days and scrubbed of direct identifiers. Dedicated/Private contracts can set custom retention windows. We support API-triggered deletion and enterprise erase workflows.

I’ve attached: redwood-exec-footprint-summary.pdf (one-page executive summary). Marissa — can you share the CSV inventory and a PNG map for Alice/Jorge?

Next step: if the committee wants us to provide SOC2 artifacts or a scoped evidence pack, we can prepare a redacted package and suggest a short call to walk through it.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-exec-footprint-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Grant <alice.grant@civicbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Ruiz <jorge@complyworks.io>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: where do requests actually run and how are they deleted?

Hi Alice / Jorge — adding the technical detail you requested. I’ve included a CSV inventory/stub plus a regional processing map (PNG). Below are the precise items your vendor manager typically looks for.

1) Subprocessor inventory (attached CSV):
- redwood inference core runtime: Redwood (self)
- Cloud compute: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), GCP (europe-west1), GCP (asia-southeast1) depending on region and customer routing
- Storage & object logs: AWS S3 / GCS (per region)
- Observability: Datadog (metrics only, metrics sanitized)
- Logging archival: S3 Glacier (encrypted) for sysadmin retention windows
- Backups / snapshots: encrypted at rest, customer keys optional via KMS

2) Regional execution patterns (short):
- Hosted API: requests routed to the nearest healthy region; primary execution clusters maintained in US-EAST-1, EU-WEST-1, APAC-SOUTHEAST-1.
- Dedicated pools: reserved capacity in a chosen cloud/region — ingress and inference stay in that region unless you opt into cross-region burst.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): execution is customer-controlled and nothing leaves the customer network unless explicitly configured.

3) Cross-border transfer notes:
- Network hops: requests traverse TLS-encrypted links between edge proxies and serving clusters; any cross-region transfer happens within our backend and is limited to routing/fallback reasons (e.g., capacity, failover).
- Data residency: we support region pinning for enterprise customers and can provide attestations for where inference occurred.

4) Retention & deletion specifics:
- KV cache: ephemeral by default; TTL 24–48 hrs. Can be configured to 0 if you require no caching.
- Customer payloads (hosted): default 30 days — configurable to shorter windows in contract.
- Operational logs: 90 days for full traces; aggregated traces retained 365 days in anonymized form for model quality and billing reconciliation (can be reduced).
- Erase workflows: API endpoint + support-assisted purge; typical completion SLA: 72 hours for hosted accounts (business-days), shorter under Dedicated/Private SLA.

5) Access control and encryption:
- All data at rest encrypted with AES-256; customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated/Private via KMS/HSM integrations.
- Role-based access control: only SREs and support engineers with just-in-time access can request session-level logs; access is audited and requires approval for retrieval of request payloads.

Attachments included: redwood-subprocessor-inventory-2027.csv, processing-map-2027.png

If the committee needs a signed attestation or a sanitized SOC2 excerpt, let us know the scope (redacted tenant names OK) and we’ll assemble a package. Happy to set a 30-minute call next week to walk through the map.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-inventory-2027.csv (csv), processing-map-2027.png (png)
From: Alice Grant <alice.grant@civicbank.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: where do requests actually run and how are they deleted?

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A couple follow-ups from our committee:

- Can you confirm whether operational logs ever contain raw customer PII, or is that redacted prior to storage? Also we need the list of Redwood roles that can access raw request payloads and the approval workflow (audit trail).
- Please provide the latest SOC2 Type II cover page and a redacted evidence index (we don’t need full reports yet, just to verify scope and status).
- Last ask: can you produce a one-page attestation that inference for CivicBank (hosted account) will be routed to EU-WEST-1 only, and describe the contractual remedy if a cross-region fallback occurs? We’ll add that to the committee packet.

If you can send the SOC2 cover page and a draft attestation by EOD Monday, that will keep us on schedule for next Friday’s committee review.

Appreciate it — Alice

--
Alice Grant
Head of Security Governance, CivicBank
